text: Frustrated. I almost never write reviews, but this has affected me in new levels and I need to write something. Been playing Battlefield since Battlefield 2. I was not able to enjoy Bad Company THAT much, but I played and kinda liked the campaign. Other than that, I "Liked" every single Battlefield game. Even Battlefield V (I still play this one, once a week). I loved Battlefield 1 (even if it is not perfect). But 2042 just hurts. Is not even good graphically, so it is not even something I can enjoy that way. Gameplay is super limited. Less weapons than any random low budget game and the few weapons we got suck. Horrible performance. Impossible matchmaking. Lack of server browser to this day (so I have to quick half of the few matches I can find due to high Ping). Portal not being part of the game, so you got the population split over there. Getting randomly kicked for no reason. Having to re-download the game every update because it fails. Horrible map design, a lot of span kills and unfair "from the other side of the map" kills. Really difficult to kill helicopters that require serious teamwork to take down (blackhawk down was 1 RPG.. 1!!!!) Good thing about the game? They "tried" some new things and that was refreshing. But instead of adding up to the battlefield experience, they removed what actually worked. Please drop this game, make a Battlefield V clone with Battlefield 1 and V maps plus 2042 maps for the giggles and give it away to the people that paid for 2042. Being a huge fan of the series I anxiously awaited the release of this game and like many others worried if my laptop would be able to play it. I was pleased to see the numerous graphic setting that allow everyone to enjoy this game. I enjoy a lot about this game, but I am still getting used to a few things and I would like to offer a few ideas and things I would like to see improved: 1. I want my worker back. I understand that you are trying to make a new game, but the roads can be an issue when the caravan just won't go the direction you want. The military engineer takes a while to get to. 2. The units are too slow. In V we were able to move across grassland and onto a mountain or cross a river. Why are we getting slower? Let's open up the battlefield for more dynamic military ability. 3. Can the AI please be programed to upgrade their units? Why am I killing catapults in 1900? This is on level 7 btw. The most difficult AI in the series was in Civ 4. 4. Does anyone miss the world congress? I do, it was a cool way to make diplomacy important even if it isn't a victory condition anymore. 5. Many of the new ideas are terrific. The card system is great. But why do the wonders suck? Where is the game changing wonder like the old Great Library, Hanging Gardens. The Teracotta army was a sick trick to play on someone. And the national wonders?

All in all, if you like the atmosphere and gameplay of Fallout 4, then you probably won't be disappointed as long as you buy this when it's heavily reduced, at maybe 75%. My advice is to wait for a free-play weekend (which occur frequently) and see if you enjoy it before taking the plunge. For me, a lot of the issue was frustration at how many easily avoided mistakes the studio made, and their lack of respect for the player-base. It takes away from the experience if I feel like the studio's trying to con me. Below is a summary of how I found it. Downsides: Poorly optimised - even on a high-end gaming computer it randomly crashes resulting in a lot of lost progress. You can't rejoin a specific server, the atom shop is actually really bad compared to paid content in other MMOs so customisation options are extremely limited, not to mention ludicrously over-priced compared to the norm. The controls aren't intuitive and many can't be re-mapped (e.g. having to go to map and then press Z to get to settings or quit), the map feels very small, and it turns into a grind-fest. The daily-ops and events stuff is too central and impacts immersion. It's like they couldn't decide whether to do a fallout game or a cookie-cutter cash-grab MMO. On the upside: The graphics are very nice, the stories have a fallout feel and there's lots of interesting bits to read / little unmarked side-stories. I've noticed some of the quests and scenes you come across have been designed by detail-oriented people who clearly care about the game. The voice-acting's good so far.

Fair amount of hours in but here are my opening thoughts Pros: -Excellent story and visuals -Honestly plays like a solo fallout game -Much like its predecessor its crafting system is solid and reasonable for the most part -Solid difficulty progression, you don't get blindsided by high level enemies with one notable exception -Large world with low loading times IN-GAME, loading into a server can take a while depending on the time of day and popularity of your C.A.M.P location. -Perks are reasonable and create a desire to have multiple characters with different skills and builds -Player economy. I like being able to buy and sell to other players as there will be ammo or Stims i do not use, but are sought after. Cons: -Depending on server load and possible other factors, its not uncommon to have trouble picking up items with long server lag. This also becomes a problem with enemies who have constantly refreshing health bars. -The stash. early on its not to much of an issue, but as you progress more and more, you have to get Obsessive Compulsive with inventory management. In my own opinion this is geared towards wanting people to buy the monthly package to have infinite junk storage (Which takes up a sizable portion of the stash) -The one exception I mentioned, If you are a low level player joining an event, and a high level player is in the vicinity, event related enemies will be notably harder from my own experience. . -Game economy. I understand WHY this is in place, but can be a little annoying. Vendors have a set amount of caps that refresh every other day or so. Unlike previous entries, you can buy and sell to pretty much trade up for what you want while working within the confines of their caps. There are significant diminishing returns when buying and selling and the price for plans can be downright absurd at times, so its often better to find a player who has them and is selling them or find them yourself if available. PVP: I have heard there can be issues with high level players preying on low levels, however in my own play most of the playerbase has been polite and even helpful by dropping supplies and plans as I was starting out.

Unpopular opinion: This game is just boring. I get that metroidvania games require a lot of backtracking, and, "where do I go next?" You gain a new ability..have to scour the map to find the one place you've unlocked with this ability..explore the new area..rinse/repeat. That's part of the genre. When you're replaying those sections, it's the sound and art that keep you from getting bored. I honestly don't remember anything about the sound, so I can't really comment on it, but the visuals...black, white and another color (blue, then green, then purple, then back to blue.) Being a blind run, I was literally falling asleep trying to navigate around to figure out where to go next, because it all looked the same. The game has a very positive review score. I'm in the minority on this one, and who knows, maybe it gets better (I stopped once I reached the city. You know...back to black/white/blue for the entire color pallete.) But there was nothing in this game to hook me into wanting to complete it, so there's no reason for me to recommend it.
